findings.title: `metrics.autoExtract` controls are added even though the description says they were removed.
findings.body:
The description says metrics auto-extract controls were dropped from this PR. The diff still adds `metrics.autoExtract` to the config type, zod schema and core types.

It also adds a new early-return branch in `emitSpanEnded` (base.ts) that skips `emitAutoExtractedMetrics`. This behaviour and public config surface are not part of the request.

findings.title: A public `signalFilters` config is added even though the description says signal filter infrastructure was removed.
findings.body:
Only the default MODEL_CHUNK drop was asked for. This adds a public per-signal filter API (spans/logs/metrics/scores/feedback) to `CloudExporterConfig`, plus hooks in every `on*Event` handler.

Once published, users will depend on this API, but the description says the design is deferred. A hard-coded MODEL_CHUNK check in `_exportTracingEvent` is enough for the request.

findings.title: The PR still ships the processor observability API its description says was removed.
findings.body:
The description says processor observability work was removed and deferred to a follow-up design. The diff still adds a public `Processor.observability` option (`false` / `'errors-only'`).

It also rewires span creation in every legacy runner path and both workflow executors, and the changeset (line 8) advertises it.

This is a new public API on shared core code that the stated request (MODEL_CHUNK drop and `warn` log default) does not cover. Either remove it, or update the request and changeset to cover it.

findings.title: TripWire aborts in the legacy runner no longer mark processor spans as errors.
findings.body:
Previously every legacy runner path called `processorSpan.error({ error, endSpan: true, ... })` on a TripWire, so blocked requests showed as ERROR in traces (the removed comment said exactly that). They now go through `span.end({ attributes })`, so the span ends as a success with no `errorInfo`.

All exporters (default storage, Langfuse, OTEL, etc.) and any error-rate dashboards or alerts will no longer see guardrail blocks as errors. This is a user-visible change unrelated to the requested volume reduction.

If you want the cloud filter to keep tripwires, keep `error()` and add `processorOutcome` as an attribute alongside it.

findings.title: Import reordering in the playground that the description says was removed.
findings.body: The description says playground import churn was removed from this PR. These import reorders, along with the matching ones in `traces/trace/index.tsx`, are unrelated to the request and should be dropped.

held.title: Dropping successful errors-only processor spans can leave their child spans orphaned in cloud.
held.body:
`'errors-only'` processors still create a span, and processor-internal work (agent or LLM calls) nests under it via `createProcessorObservabilityContext`.

The cloud filter drops only the PROCESSOR_RUN span itself, so the children are still uploaded with a `parentSpanId` that never arrives. That can produce broken trees or orphaned spans in the cloud UI.

I could not check how the cloud backend handles a missing parent. Consider dropping the descendants too, or re-parenting them.
